finding: write_atomic still cannot replace a read-only file on Windows, and the test of that case is skipped there.
why: A read-only `~/.claude/settings.json` or `CLAUDE.md` on Windows makes `os.replace(tmp, path)` raise `[WinError 5] Access is denied` (two reviewers probed it), so a takeover or switch-back fails midway while POSIX succeeds.
fix: Clear the read-only bit on the target before `os.replace`, keep the mode, and test it on Windows too.
evidence: os.replace(tmp, path)  /  @pytest.mark.skipif(os.name == "nt", reason="POSIX file modes")  def test_write_atomic_replaces_a_read_only_file_and_keeps_its_mode

finding: A failed write (disk full, I/O error) leaves the temp file behind, because cleanup covers only the copymode and replace step.
why: `out.write(data)` raising ENOSPC leaves a partial `.afkv2-tmp` that can hold a secret; the failure test only injects an `os.replace` error.
fix: Put the open and write inside the `try`, and add a test where the write raises.

finding: The privacy test asserts the argument passed to os.open, not that the temp file is private when the data sits in it.
why: It passes on Windows, where the mode is ignored, breaks on a refactor of the open call, and never checks the temp file's mode when shutil.copymode runs.
fix: Spy on shutil.copymode, read the temp file's mode and bytes at that moment, and assert no group or other bits are set (skip on nt); for a new file assert the umask-derived final mode.
evidence: def spy(path, flags, *args, **kwargs): modes.append(args[0]) ... assert modes == [mode] and target.read_bytes() == b"token\r\n"

criterion: changed defaults / accepted-input set of a shared helper (plugins._read_json)
finding: _read_json refuses a falsy non-object `enabledPlugins` (`[]`, `""`, `0`, `false`), which blocks a takeover, and the choice is nowhere recorded.
why: The reader runs on the user, project and local layers, so a shared settings.json with such a value now stops takeover through `_check_plugin_inputs`.
fix: Record the tightening in DECISIONS.md as deliberate.

finding: The retry advice is wrong when the git failure is permanent.
why: A broken repository or a persistent ownership error keeps the answer `failed` and the install record stays, while the reason says only 'run switch-back again'.
fix: Name the cause and what to fix first, for example git access to the repository (safe.directory).
evidence: reason="git could not name the ignore file; run switch-back again")
